newsitem.title: USA: Gulf Coast refiners prepare for possible storm hit.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Coast refiners prepare for possible storm hit.

text.p: Gulf Coast refiners who are possibly in the path of Tropical Storm Danny are in initial stages of preparing for the storm's landfall, now expected late Thursday or early Friday.
But oil company spokespersons said that while initial precautionary measures are underway, the facilities are far from cutting back or shutting down their plants.
Exxon Corp for example, which operates a huge 432,000 barrel per day (bpd) refinery at Baton Rouge, is taking precautions but does not foresee any problems.
"In regard to the Baton Rouge refinery, high winds are not expected that far inland, but precautions have been made to tie down or bring in loose materials," Exxon spokesman Dave Gardner said.

Chevron Corp's Pascagoula, Miss., refinery, which is near the eastern end of the National Hurricane Center's hurricane watch area, has also begun storm preparations, but a spokesman declined to comment in detail on its plans ahead of the storm.

"We are operating," said Steve Renfroe, a spokesman at Chevron's 295,000 barrel per day Pascagoula, Miss., refinery, adding that it was a "possibility" the refiery could close if the storm bears down on western Mississippi.
The National Hurricane Center in Miami said rains from Danny were already pelting the Lousiana coast and the storm could strengthen before hitting land late Thursday or early Friday.
A tropical storm warning and hurricane watch stretched from Cameron, Louisiana to Orange Beach, Alabama, and rains of five to 10 inches (13 to 25 cm) could accompany the storm, it said.

British Petroleum, which operates a 240,000 bpd refinery at Belle Chasse, Lousiana said it had entered the second of five emergency planning fives which involves precautionary measures like tying loose items down.
Marathon Oil Co said it is monitoring the storm to see if it threatens its 225,000 bpd Garyville, Lousisiana plant.

Other refineries that are possibly in the storm's path include Mobil Corp's 176,000 bpd Chalmette, Louisiana refinery, Shell Oil Co's 218,000 bpd Norco, Lousisiana and the Star's 230,000 bpd Convent, Louisiana refinery.

The storm, packing winds of 60 miles per hour (96.56 kilometres per hour, was centered about 100 miles southwest of New Orleans, and was moving in a northeastern direction at 5 miles per hour (8.047 kph).
The eye of the storm was expected to make landfall late Thursday or early on Friday.
